title: Frame moves between same-colour parts: trimmed from about 2.3 mm, sewn across below
description: Six 5 x 5 mm red fill squares with gaps of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 mm (needle-to-needle moves of about 2.2, 3.2, 4.1, 5.1 and 7.1 mm): PE-DESIGN 11.50 trims the four longer moves and sews the 1 mm gap across as a plain stitch, so there is no untrimmed jump in the file. The squares' y position is OpenStitch's choice (PE imported them centred); only the moves matter. OpenStitch's optimized exit and entry points lie on the squares' edges where PE-DESIGN's lie 0.5 mm inside them and 1 mm apart in y (its moves are sqrt((gap + 1)^2 + 1) mm), so the squares are drawn at PE-DESIGN's needle-to-needle moves and the trimming rule is compared at equal moves; where PE puts its exit and entry inside the edge is the fill track's open item.

evidence.note: PE-DESIGN 11.50 reference machine/machine-jumps.pes (pe-refs-3, 2026-10-28): 525 stitches, 4 trims on moves of 3.16, 4.12, 5.10 and 7.07 mm, the 1 mm gap a plain stitch, 0 colour changes.

references.make: Import an SVG (100 x 100 mm) with six 5 x 5 mm red squares at x = 10, 16, 23, 31, 40, 51 mm (gaps 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 mm), as Fill Stitch at PE-DESIGN's import defaults (multi-needle machine type, Jump Stitch Trimming on); change nothing. Save with Save As as PES (PE-DESIGN 11's default PES version) under the file name given, and record the PE-DESIGN version, the date, the operating system and every setting you changed in compat/reference/MANIFEST.json (see docs/COMPATIBILITY_TESTS.md).

measurements.evidence: every interior move is a trimmed jump (as many moves as trims); a gap PE-DESIGN does not trim is sewn across as a stitch, never left as a plain jump
PE-DESIGN's count (its fill rows join differently from OpenStitch's, the text-fill item of the audit)
